`addMove` expands into 4 promotion moves when the destination `to` is on the promotion rank (rank 8 for white = RANK_1 index 7, rank 1 for black = RANK_8 index 0). My guard is applied *before* `addMove` is called (on the single-step advance), and it only excludes off-board `to`. All promotion moves are addressed to on-board squares, so structurally there's no interaction. But I'll verify empirically.

Plan:
1. Write a verification script: white pawns on all 8 files of rank 7 (with the target square empty), plus edge-file capture promotions (a7×b8, h7×g8), plus, for symmetry, black pawns on rank 2 (a2→a1=Q, etc., and the edge captures a2×b1, h2×g1). Confirm that each generates exactly the expected 4 promotion SANs.
2. Add regression tests for the key cases (all files, or at least the edge files — the user said "pawns on rank 7," so cover all 8 files for white's rank 7. That's the direct request. For completeness also include the black rank 2 mirror. Since we previously discovered that a vacuous black subcase was a trap).

Wait — mind the turn: a white pawn on rank 7 needs white to move; a black pawn on rank 2 needs black to move. Use a FEN with kings placed to make it legal, e.g. `4k3/P7/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1` — hmm, but a white pawn on a7 with the white king on e1 and the black king on e8: promotion on a7→a8... no problem. But wait, if it's white to move in `4k3/P7/...`, the white pawn on a7: a8 is empty → 4 promotion moves. Kings don't interfere.

For all 8 files: place one pawn at a time. E.g. FEN `4k3/P7/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1` (a7), then b7, etc. Or more simply: use the `chess.put` approach on a board with kings: start from `4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1`, then `put({type:'p',color:'w'}, 'a7')`.

Capture promotions: `4k3/P6p/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1`? h7 has a black pawn... then the white pawn on g7? No wait — I want to test the edge-file capture a7×b8: a white pawn on a7, an enemy piece on b8. `2p3k1/P7/...`? b8 = pawn? Let me construct: black king on e8, black pawn on b8, white pawn on a7, white king on e1: FEN `1p2k3/P7/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1`. Then a7: a8 (promotion, 4) + a7×b8 (promotion capture, 4) = 8 moves. Edge file h7×g8 is the mirror.

Expected SANs (from an empty context, no disambiguation needed):
- a7→a8: a8=N, a8=B, a8=R, a8=Q (order is PROMOTIONS = [n, b, r, q]). Check suffix: does a8=Q give check? White king on e1, black king on e8. Queen on a8 — a8→e8 diagonal? a8, b7, c6... no, that's the a8-h1 diagonal: b7, c6, d5, e4, f3, g2, h1. Not e8. Rank 8: a8..e8 — are there any pieces on b8-c8-d8? No (b8 is empty in this variant) → Qa8 checks along rank 8! So a8=Q gets a `+`. Similarly a8=R also checks on rank 8 (a8→b8→c8→d8→e8 clear) → a8=R+. a8=N: a knight on a8 attacks b6, c7 — no check. a8=B: the a8-h1 diagonal doesn't include e8; no check.

Hmm, this makes the exact SAN expected values position-dependent. To keep the test simple and robust, I'll use a position where no checks arise. E.g., put the black king on h4? Hmm, but then the king might attack the promotion square... let me place the kings far away: black king a4? Then a white queen on a8 is... a4-a8 is the same file! The simplest: use a position like the ones existing promotion tests use. Let me see how is-promotion.test.ts and move.test.ts handle this.
